l1.why: ج head with dot below, و loop, a tooth (ن/ک merged) and final ه bowl = چونکه; no ش teeth or ن dot for nişân

و, tall ا, ه, final ب with dot below

l1.why: ف(dot)+ر, م loop + ا (w11), ن (w12), ف(dot)+ر+م+ا (w13), round ی (w14); written as fermân + fermâ-y pieces
ن dot, ظ with tall stem and dot, م with long descending tail
م, two teeth with dots below (ب ی), final ن
و, ط with tall stem, ه, ر; shadda over ه
three teeth with dots (ب ی ت) and final ی, written small and stacked above وطهّر
two lams, ط loop with shadda, 'ائفین' written small above the ط
و loop (end of w18), alif-lam, ق loop, 'ائمین' stacked above with hamza mark
و with long tail, alif-lam, ر with shadda, ک with shadda (w19b), big final ع bowl (w20)
three tall verticals: ا (w21), ل (w22), first tall tooth of س; then س teeth with shadda, ج with dot below, و, د (w23)
م, ح, ض with dot above
tall ا, م loop at baseline, ر as a very long sweep that returns up as a hairline ending in the blob of w26
the left upright of the pair has a counter (medial ه loop) and the final ی joins it, which ا could not do; so لهی after an isolated ا, not لا+ی
isolated و
tall ل, ط loop with stem, final ف with ه-like tail
right piece is plainly ن(dot) ا م ت ن(dots) ا; the high closed loop after it is the initial ه of -hî; the لطف to the right fits lutf-ı nâ-mütenâhî
the outline holds only a dot; the word is the low cluster below (long stretched س stroke, two teeth with dots below, short ل, final hook) which lies inside w31m's outline
م head with ن dot above, long stretched ش stroke with two stacked dots beside it, و loop; the ر sits in w34's outline; same build as w35m
left piece: flat خ head with dot above, two joined uprights (لا), a head with dot (ف), zigzag ت + final tick; right piece is the ر of w33

Small hooked م head at upper right with a single dot just above it (ن), long thin stretched stroke down-left carrying the 3-dot caret (ش), then clear و and ر at the baseline. The shapes do say menşûr again, not 've'/tevkî‘. Because خلافه stands right before it, it may be the compound adjective 'hilâfet-menşûr' and not a second izafet noun.

Stretched س stroke coming from upper right, tall ل, ط loop, then teeth with one dot (ن) and one dot (ت, two dots written as one), ending in a big round final ی bowl. I see no extra tooth or loop for م, so not -ımı. The final ی is either accusative or izafet -ı.
ع head with dot of ن above, و loop, tall ا, short final ن hook; the 'counter' on the upright is the ن/و join
ف head with dot, خ head with its own dot higher up, tooth (ی), small م, final ه

a single long stroke from a small hook (dot above it) sweeping down-left, a small ء/sîn-sign-like mark beside it (w41), then a thin hairline bowl rising to a second small head (w42/w43a); same stretched-stroke + sign pattern the scribe uses for س/ش, but I cannot assemble a word; may be only an izafet/flourish before the quoted title
flat wedge head with dot above (خ, not the oblique dîvânî ک), joined tall ا, small د and م with long tail down-left
tall alif-lam loop, ح turning back, ر, small م, tooth with dot below (ی), short final; kerîme fits the compressed shapes no better and follows Hâdim poorly
tall alif-lam loop running into a long descending stroke with the small şîn sign above it, ر, ف with dot above, ی with two dots below, final ن; completes Hâdimü’l-Haremeyni’ş-Şerîfeyn
only one tall letter (alif-lam loop), one crossing tooth with dot below (ب), then a non-joining 3-shaped د; no ق dots, no second ل, no final ه for lakabıyla
l1.note: one word over two outlines (w49m + w51a), per verifier and adjudicator

l1.why: a new piece starting high (as after non-joining د) with a long ی kesîde and dots beside it, ending in a final ع/ج bowl; no teeth or و for tetvîc; the dot under the bowl would favour ج, so doubtful
l1.note: end of el-bedî‘, text carried by w49m

l1.why: isolated و at the left edge of w51

Descending ر stroke at the right, then a tooth with two dots stacked above it (ت), then a tooth with one dot below (ب), then a final ه with a short tail at the left. This is a noun (rütbe), not a verbal noun or participle as the hint expects.
isolated و

initial stroke with a raised pointed loop (ک+ع), the only dot is below the third tooth (ب), final ه; behiyye would put the dot under the first tooth, Beyt has no final ه; Ka‘be-i Mu‘azzama is the set phrase
م/ع heads, ظ = loop + tall stem with dot, م, then a large terminal loop with a very long sweep (end-of-line flourish in the stack); final ه uncertain

l2.why: short initial stroke (ت) then ر descending, a loop with two dots above and one dot below: dots fit ت+ب of تربه; روضه has no dot below and only one ض dot. The formulary's ravza-i does not match the dots
م, ط loop with ascender, ه, ر, final ة with two dots
ح head, teeth with one + two dots below (ب ی), final ب as rising stroke with dot below
alif, slanted ک bar, ر, م, then an extra small hook with a dot above after م; a bare اکرم leaves that final hook unexplained (genitive ـك/ڭ, dot = kâf-ı nûnî mark)
long ک bar over م+ا, then teeth with a dot below and dots above (ی ن ب), غ hook with dot above, large final ی bowl
خ with dot above + د, then م, a tooth and a clear final ـه hook: the ه rules out bare hıdmet; the ت/ن teeth are merged so the exact ending is uncertain

و at the lower right, then a tall looped alif-lam, an ع head (open loop), a tooth with one dot below (ب), a tall alif, and a small final د+ة at the left. These are the letters of والعبادة. There is no medial ی/ی+ت cluster for 'ubûdiyye. The odd grammar does not change what is written.
tall ا, ل, ا, a ز hook with its dot above, م with long dîvânî tail, faint ة with two dots; the dot sits on the ز, not on a final ن
isolated و
ح head + ر form one detached piece, then a new piece م-tooth-ن with the dot over the final ن; in حضرت the ض would be joined to ح, not after a break
tall ا/ل with a ج bowl and its dot below, tall ل, tooth, looped ل, final ه, all in one connected group; no word break or ا as جل جلاله would need
interlinear word starts with an open flick (ت) not a closed م loop, then an ع bump, a tall looped ا/ل, and a dark final ی blob at the foot; معلا would end in a free ا
small separate و loop at baseline, two filled loops (ف/ق) with one dot above, then a short free ا at left; no ب dot below and no final ه as بقعه needs
faint: a long slanted stroke rising to the right (dîvânî س or reversed ی?), a small ع/ک-like hook, then a م/ع head with a long descending tail; no dots; no word recognised
short د hook (stray dot above), و, tall ل, final ت drawn as a ـه loop with a dot; an extra small loop before the ل leaves some doubt
the long slanted stroke rises out of معد (it is ل+ت of ma‘delet, not a free ک head), then two teeth, an ا, and an ending with a dot below that looks like ـیه more than ـت
tall alif, a long faint slanted stroke down-left, and a small faint hook further left; no dots
ا ل ه loop, tooth with a dot, a small ه-like hook below and a ی bowl; the extra tooth and the hook do not fit bare ilâhî
head loop with a dot plus a descending و-tail that seems to join the following teeth (a final ی of فی would not join), tooth with dot above (ف), dot below (ی), loop (ق), rising ا and end hook
ص head, then م and د bumps before the tall looped ا, then ن dot above, ی dot below, final ه; the م+د bumps between head and ا are too many for کلائه
isolated و
tall ا, a dot above, a tall looped ل/ط, then a final with a closed loop head and baseline tail (ف, not open-headed ع); the middle letters are compressed
ب dot below, tall لا loop, small ـیه at left, plus a raised نا/تا group with dots at upper right inside the outline; bilâdihi leaves the raised group unexplained
separate و, then ع head, ط with tall ascender, ف loop with dot above, rising ا and a final ت hook; the ط ascender does not fit ووفاقه
long dîvânî س keşide, dot below (ب) before a thick ح blob, then a tooth with dot above (ن) and final ه; compressed, but dot order ب…ن fits sübhâniyye and the following -sine
long keşide ending in a small ه loop with one dot above-left (ن); no ع and no ب dot below as کعبه needs
م head, ظ loop with ascender and dot above, ه, final descending ر; no second م loop or final ه for معظمه
و
loop head with dot above (ق/ف), ر, tooth with dot below (ی), final ن hook whose dot sits just left; the و lies outside the outline, and karîn fits 'mazhar ve karîn buyurduğu'
ب dot below, ی, و, ر, د, ی, غ, final ی bowl

Tall looped alif/lam joined in dîvânî fashion to a tooth with one dot below (ب), then separate د, then و, then ل and a final ه with a dot/pair above that I take as the merged ت of devlet + dative -e; no mim or other letters for a 'devlet-i ...' or 'saltanatıma' reading. The shapes stay ebed + devlete, even though the grammar expects something else.
و, ر, و, ض with dot, final ه, two dots after it
faint cluster with a ط-like ascender, loops and a descending tail after 've Ravza-i'; the overall shape fits مطهره but no letter can be seen clearly
ج head with dot below, long bowl with dot above (ن); the tall ا and final ب with dot below just left complete جناب

flagged tall ک stroke, then a و loop, then a tooth with dot above (ن), tooth with dot below (ی), final نه; the و comes before the dotted teeth, the reverse of النبویه. سید is written just right, outside the outline
l2.note: adjudicator: الکونینه inside the outline, سید written just right of it; Seyyid not read on its own

l2.why: a closed horizontal loop (ص) joined to a tall ل with a foot; a ح head would be an open cup, not a closed loop; fits the eulogy after Seyyidü’l-Kevneyn
l2.note: the abbreviated eulogy sallallâhu ‘aleyhi ve sellem; brackets removed

l2.why: Two dots above the first tooth (ت), a ج hook with a dot below, then د, a ی tooth with a dot below, and a final د. This is tecdîd, not hıdmet: there is no خ head and no م/ت ending. With w60 it forms the pair 'tecdîd ü ibkâ'.

Tall loop with a bowl joined on its left that has a clear dot BELOW (ب, not the bare ل of القا), then a loop head with a dot above (ق/ف), then a final alif stroke. The dot below rules out ilkâ. It is a bare verbal noun ('tecdîd [ü] ibkâ'), not a finite verb. Any 'olunmak/kılınmak' must be in the next word, not in this box.

l3.why: body is two upright looped strokes on the baseline + small final ه = لله; the floating hooked stroke above is one of a regular run of such strokes (one here, one over w02, two over w04) that read as ال of the following words rather than kef bars; the small mark at the left is too weak to be a ف dot

floating stroke above = ا/ل; body = hooked head with filled loop (ح+م) then descending stroke; but the end is a hooked ج/ی-like curl with a clear dot below, which fits neither د nor a kerîm final م, so only the set phrase lillâhi'l-hamd ve'l-minne tips it

two floating strokes directly above = ال, و loop at right, ح-like لمـ ligature, tooth (ن) and final ه; a clear dot sits below the ح-like shape, which would favour ج (vechih), but vechih leaves the two strokes above unexplained
tooth with two stacked dots below, short ascender, ر-stroke, then a final م with descender just outside the outline (…یلرم); no word can be verified from this skeleton

long diagonal from top right sweeping into a hairline with the small detached caret mark above, then bowl, loop with dot above and final upright ا; the same caret recurs on the ş of ferâşet (w26) and 'ş-şân (w61d), so read as ش dots; next words 'llâhu te‘âlâ confirm inşâ'allâh
tall stroke + big closed loop with inner hairline (لله ligature shape), tail to the left; previous reader's ba'd has no ascender, this has one
small ت head with dot above, ع, tall ا, ل, final ی returning right
one tall looped upright (ا/ل written together) descending into a bowl that curls back inward = final ی; ilâ yevmi'l-âhire
tooth with a dot below (ی), small closed و loop, then م with the long hooked descender; no second tooth for nebî
tall ا, ل, خ with dot above, ر down-stroke, then a small closed loop without tail = final ه
ح loop, ر, م with long curved descender
م head, ح, ت tooth with dot, ر, then one small closed loop = final م; no separate م before a ه, so muhtereme lacks a letter
isolated و loop with tail
loop with a dot above (ح/خ) then a ی tail swung down and back right; the و loop next to it may be the separate ve; no ج, ر or ه for Hücre
م head, medial ه as a ح-like descender, ب tooth with dot below, then closed loop with tall upright at its left = ط; two short marks above the upright are not explained (they would suit ة/ق)
toothed ع head, م, و loop, final م with long hooked descender; tall stroke to its left is the ا of the next word

ال uprights, small ع hook, tooth with dot above (ت), tooth with dot below (ب), upright ا, final ت drawn as a ط-like loop; the outline also runs on over the ferâşet body (ف loop with dot, long ا, flat ش with caret), so B's ve gâh is that word
the outline holds only the small caret above the flat hairline: the dîvânî three-dot sign of ش in ferâşet, whose body (ف, ر, long ا, flat ش, final ت) lies inside w26a's outline; followed by şerîfe
ش teeth with stacked dots above, ر, ی dot below, ف loop with dot, final ه
tooth with dots, ر stroke, second tooth with dot, tooth with dot below (ی), long open final ب bowl; the small loop inside is the separate ve; tertîb ve tanzîm pairing
small isolated و
two teeth with single dots above (ت ن), tall ظ upright with loop and dot, ی with dot below, م, then a dotted tooth before the final ه = -ine; no ع head before the ظ
ح, م, د, ا with two-stroke tanwin above
single ٤-like ligature with two dots stacked above it, between two hamdan (the tanwîn marks over each hamdan are visible); ثمّ fits hamden sümme hamden
same shape as w32, tanwin strokes above
م head into و bowl, two loops each with a dot above (ف ق), tooth with dot below and further teeth, final ه; there is no ل upright, so min kıbelihi lacks its lâm; the exact ending is uncertain

Clear mîm head, then خ with its dot above, a lâm shaft, a ص loop, and a short final hook (alif of the tanwîn, or ه). The shapes give مخلص, not a noun such as şükr or hamd, so I keep the adverb even though the hint wants a subject.
long rising kef stroke with the small mark above, low tooth, ر, then a tooth with the dot below it after the ر, then upright ا; the ی dot after ر fits کبریا, kesîran would put it before ر
لا loop, ز with dot above, م with long descender
ب tooth with dot below + و loop
floating diagonal kef bar above a tall looped ک body, ر sweep, and the small detached final ه just left; follows bu

Mîm head, then غ with its dot above, then a descending stroke for ف (its dot is probably the loose one beside it), ر, and a final round ه/ة. This is مغفرة/مغفرت. The shapes do not show a vacancy noun such as fevt or ferâğ, so I keep mağfiret.
hooked head at top, long diagonal ر, then a stacked pair of dots (ی) and an open final ن bowl; the shapes do not show و-ف-ا-ت, so vefâtı is ruled out
و, ق with dots, و, open ع with long tail
two tall uprights (ا, ل) and an open ح-like curl at the end that reads as dîvânî final ه or ی; the shapes fit both, so the formulary vukû‘ıyla decides
detached و, tall ا, ق loop with two dots above, ٤-shaped ع
hooked ح head, ا, crossed dîvânî لا with its loop; the dot sits under the left loop, not under the head, so not a ج dot; same word as w54
two joined round loops (ح, ص), the ص tooth, then a short final ه tail; no dots; ‘uhde fits the same loops
open ‘ayn head with eye, short ل upstroke, one ی tooth with dot below, final ه hook; too few teeth for ‘ayniyye

small م head, ر sweep that breaks the word, then the detached -tbe group (tooth + final ه) just left of the outline (the piece that w54's outline swallowed); seniyye would be one unbroken run of teeth
hooked ح head, ا, crossed لا with long loop; no dot under the head; the small detached له below-right is the end of mürettebe, not part of this word; hâlâ Hazîne-i Hâssam nâzırı
خ with dot above, ز dot, ی/ن teeth with dots, final ه

letter by letter: hooked head with a clear dot above = خ; narrow tall loop = ا; small closed loop = ص; long descender curling down and right = final م (as in yevm, w13); the dot rules out ح for Hilmî; Hazîne-i Hâssa(m) is an office, not a personal name
ن dot, ا, ظ with tall stroke and dot, ر, final ی bowl
first word of the stack: hooked ا running into flattened teeth with dots (ی ش), ب dot below, small و loop at the bottom; no ف loop or ع
l3.note: l3 adjudicator: râfi‘ is the small group between işbu and tevkî‘, inside no outline; it sits with w61a's ink

l3.why: ت with dot, و loop, ق loop with dot above, ی tooth with dot below, final ع bowl; râfi‘ is the smaller group below this outline, between işbu and this word
detached small ر at right, ف loop with dot above, ی tooth with dot below, final ع bowl
loop with flag at top (ال), long descending stroke with the detached caret beside it = ش (same caret as in inşâ and ferâşet); first part of 'ş-şân, split across the stack; refî‘ is w61c
l3.note: l3 adjudicator: w61d and w61e together read ’ş-şân-ı (الش / ان)

l3.why: flagged head at top then a long curved stroke ending in a small upturn = final ن bowl, completing 'ş-şân-ı before hâkânî; hümâyûn-ı hâkânî is not the formula
l3.note: second half of ’ş-şân-ı, text carried by w61d

l3.why: خ dot above, ا, ق dots, ا, ن, ی; followed by the long terminal flourish up the margin

l4.why: Hollow tall stroke whose foot runs into the next letter; this hand does that with a lone alif too (w54a اول). Then a loop with a dot above (ف), a pair of dots (ت), a bowl (خ, its dot not clear) and a detached ر, which is what a preceding alif causes. Shapes alone lean slightly to el-fakîr, but w03 carries its own ال, so the izafet head iftihâr fits the line.
Hollow ال loop, ‘ayn head, a tall slanted alif and a detached low ی tail. The two readings differ by one alif that this hand would merge, so the formulaic e‘âlî is taken.
isolated و

Hollow ال loop, ‘ayn with an open eye, a stroke rising to a hooked upright with a dot above (ظ), then a final م squiggle at the lower left. The dot sits over the upright, not over the ‘ayn, which argues against غ.

NAME, letter by letter: a long rising keşide with the small curled three-dot sign above (ش; the same sign is on the şâyân keşide in w47); a loop with a square dot above (ف); a tooth with one dot below (ی); a small final closed loop with a short tail and no dots visible (ق). A dot over the loop rules out ‘ayn, so Ka‘be does not fit.
Short base tooth with one dot below (ب), then a long rising diagonal with the dîvânî kef hook halfway up (ک). It follows the name, and dâme ‘ulüvvühû comes next.
Looped د, a tall pointed loop for the alif, then a م loop with its tail swinging down to the left. This is the standard dâme before ‘ulüvvühû.
Faint crown-shaped ‘ayn head at the top right, a dark و loop, and the small final ه. cûh only describes the visible fragment; ‘ulüvvühû completes dâme.

R to L: loop with dot above = ف, descending ر, tall alif, closed loop with dot above = medial غ, small tooth with dot above = ن, final ـه tail; dative ferâğına (Ottoman spelling with ه). Fits the ferâğ hint; the shapes alone suggest it, the غ dot is the only doubt
ف with a dot, ر, a faint alif along the crease, then a long keşide with three scattered dots above (ش) and the ت drawn like ـه. It has the same shape as ferâşet later in the line.

teeth with dots above = ش, ر, single dot below = ی, loop with dot above = ف, then ـه, a small د-hook and a final ـه curl with no dot and no ن bowl. Reads as locative -de, not the ablative -den the hint expects: no ن is visible
ب dot below + ر
Head with a dot above at the right (ق), ی with a dot below, a tall alif, and a ط upright with a closed loop at its base. The dot above the head rules out ج/celâl.
ع, ه and looped د, ه, then the long rising س keşide and ـنه with a dot. It has the same shape as ‘uhdesine at w41-w42; ‘an covers only the first hump.
Faint word in the context box: a dot over a hook, a bowl, a crown-shaped ج, teeth (ی ه), then a curve with a dot above (ن) and ی. Too faint for more than a guess.
A closed loop with a short separate upright above it (ط) and a wide final ب sweep, with no clear tooth or dot for a ن. Both readings fit the loop; taleb ve istid‘â is the formula.
small و written under the long diagonal; the same candidate holds the alif + س keşide + ت of the next word (split)

A hollow tall alif (this hand's alif, as in w54a), a long س keşide, a tooth with one dot (ت), a looped د like the و-shaped د elsewhere, then a faint ع and alif curl. en-nebevî also fits the strokes, but it makes no sense between taleb ve and eylediğine binâen.

Hollow alif with a closed loop at its foot, a faint upright (ل/ک), a tooth, and ـنه with dots above. el-‘aliyye fits the opening loop equally well, but this hand also draws alif+letter as a hollow loop, and binâ’en follows.
The outline holds only a dot, but the gap before بر has a dot below (ب), a short upright with a dot above (ن) and a faint alif. These are faint, so this is only a guess.
بر (in w32) + و loop + ج with dot below + ه; the long swash above belongs to the next word
ح hook at the top of the long swash (in w33), swash = س keşide, ب dot below, closed ی loop (w34)
ب with dot below + ر
ق with dot, ی dot below, ر, alif, ط upright with loop; leftmost ف loop belongs to the next word
ف (in w36) with dot, ر, faint alif, long ش keşide with two/three dots, ت ending
rising ش with three dots, ر, ی dot below, ف loop with dot, ه

detached suffix: long stroke from upper right with small teeth at the top (س), one dot over the descending tooth (ن), ending in a returning ی hook at the bottom; no final ه or second ن, so not -sine. Shapes say -sini despite the hint that it's odd after a quantity phrase
ع ه د in w41; the separate ه, long س keşide and ـنه with dot are in the right part of w42 (split)
Crown-shaped ج head, a tooth with a dot below (ی), ه, and a final ی bowl, the same shape as tevcîh earlier. B covers only the final bowl.
خ head with dot above, ص loop, و, ص loop, ن dot, ه (all in w43 except the ی bowl at its right, which ends tevcîhi)
A club-headed long stroke (م head and س keşide), a faint alif arc, then a clear عده at the left. The outline's single shaft is part of this word, not a word of its own.
Faint crown-shaped initial ‘ayn, a tooth with a dot below (ی), ه with an eye, and م with a long tail. cîhim fits the same strokes, but müsâ‘ade-i ‘aliyyem is the formula.
Long rising keşide with the curled three-dot sign above (ش), alif, ی with one dot, a faint alif, and a small final ن. B describes only the shaft.
Hollow diagonal alif with a dark junction (و/ل), the same opening as اول in w54a; then a loop with a dot above (غ) and a final ی bowl with a dot below. Medenî makes no sense between şâyân and hâlde.
Crown-shaped ح, a faint alif, a zigzag ل, a descending د and a final oval ه. The two-part ending is ده, not a single alif.
In the straightened crop: a hollow tall alif, a dark closed و loop with an eye, and a wide ل bowl. There is no kef knot.
A small compressed group: a dot below (ب), a short headed upright (ا/ب), and an oval (ه/د). There is no dot above for the ز of yüz. ol bâbda continues the sentence.
two tall verticals joined at the foot = لا, then separate ز with a dot above, then a small م with a tail; only two verticals, so there is no extra alif for an el- article
A slanted kef stroke above a dark small loop, a faint ل, and a bowl (ن). It follows el-lâzım; no ی dots for yedi.
Only a very long curved stroke with a small hook and a faint ring at the top of the stack; no dots and no letters can be identified.

l5.why: Short tooth with one dot clearly below (ب/ی), then a tall looped ascender (ل), then a small final ه hook going left. No other teeth or loops that would make a noun. The shapes give bile and I keep it against the hint.

long keşide with two stacked dots above (ت), a short upstroke and bowl, a loop with one dot above (ف/ض), then a tall back-curled ل ending the word; the single dot below is unexplained; no ش teeth or final م, so şerîfim does not fit

looped tall stroke joined at its foot to a closed ص loop, then a second tall looped stroke, then a reversed-C final ی; no د between loop and second stem, so ısdârı does not fit; the first stroke joins forward, so it is ال written as one stroke
خ with dot above, ص loop, و, ص loop, final ی
م head, tooth with dot above (ن), ح with a dot below it (may be stray or belong to the ن), tall ل ending in a flat leftward tail; no اولمغله follows in the same word
one short downstroke (د) then a closed ـه loop; no tall stem, so not له
ب with dot below, wedge ح head, long slanted alif, tall stem ending in a big looped ل; no extra final alif after the loop
ح head merging into a large closed loop (ص) then a short tail with a small final ـه at left; the ـه tail rules out بو
eyed head with a flick to the right joins without a break into the teeth (initial ع; و would not join), teeth with one dot below (ب), final ـه
wedge head descending into ر, then a separate group of a tooth and final ـه: two pieces only, while اوزره would need four (ا|و|ز|ره); dots not visible
ح head hooked at the top right, alif, closed لا loop
alif, و, ق loop with dot above, alif, ف loop
ه loop, م, ی with dot below, و loop, ن; the final م is written above as a raised hook
